title: Repeated Timing with Correctness Check
adaptationNote: The timing loop still runs, but its variable median is displayed as a nonnegative-duration check. Use original.cpp to inspect actual nanosecond measurements; this is not a speed assertion.

guide.problem: Keep algorithm answers correct while studying memory access cost.
guide.design: Contiguous traversal can use caches well. A benchmark explores cost but cannot establish correctness or guarantee a speedup.
guide.invariant: Alternative traversals compute the same checksum; timing units and workload are clear.
guide.failure: One noisy run is not a stable speed claim. Removing a checksum can let optimization discard the work.
guide.trace: A 2x2 row-major buffer [1,2,3,4] visits 1,2,3,4 by rows and 1,3,2,4 by columns; both sum to 10.
guide.maintenance: Use repeated measurements, documented hardware/compiler options, and independent result checks.
guide.scope: This panel connects this listing to its chapter’s problem. Short demonstrations illustrate one part; the chapter’s complete implementation and invariant labs test the broader contract.
